subject: [PATCH v1 2/2] mm/memory: add anonymous mTHP folios to deferred split list

reviews.author: Barry Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer Barry Song questioned whether khugepaged_max_ptes_none should be set to 16 (order-4) for a base page size of 64KB, suggesting that this would allow splitting when there are 17 or more zero PTEs and collapsing when there are 16 or fewer. He also proposed using different thresholds for splitting and collapse with the splitting threshold higher than the collapse threshold to avoid thrashing around the threshold.
reviews.raw_body:
thanks for the clarification, Usama, Johannes.

For your case, where the base page size is 64KB, you want to split
a 2MB mTHP, which is order-5. So would you have
khugepaged_max_ptes_none to 16 (i.e., order-4)?

So, for example, once you have 17 or more zero PTEs, you split the
folio. And if you have 16 or fewer zero PTEs, you collapse it?

If so, it seems Johannes's proposal might be the simplest way to
go.

BTW, do you see any issue around 16? To me, it seems more
sensible to use different thresholds for splitting and collapse,
with the splitting threshold higher than the collapse threshold.
That way, there is some hysteresis between the two, avoiding
thrashing around the threshold.

2026-08-05.patch_summary: This patch adds anonymous memory huge pages (mTHP folios) to the deferred split list in the mm/memory module, allowing for more efficient handling of THPs and reducing the likelihood of OOMs due to poor virtual packing. The change is motivated by issues with existing services that thrashed and ran out of memory when enabling 2M pages. By making it possible to run with THPs enabled, this patch aims to simplify the management of memory huge pages and improve system performance.
